title: Catch it and keep going
summary: try and catch handle an exception; finally runs no matter what.

say.never: Put code that might throw inside a `try { }` block. After it, a `catch` block says which kind of exception you can handle. If the try block throws that kind, Java jumps straight to the catch block and the program carries on. If nothing is thrown, the catch block is skipped. `Integer.parseInt("12")` turns text into a number, but `Integer.parseInt("twelve")` throws a `NumberFormatException`, so it's a good thing to try.
say.bit: `try { ... } catch (SomeException e) { ... }`: if the try block throws that kind, the catch block runs instead of a crash.

say.never: Sometimes the best thing a catch block can do is throw a *better* exception: one that says what went wrong in your program's own words. The caller then only has to handle one kind. Catch blocks can be stacked; Java uses the first one that fits.
say.bit: A catch block can throw your own exception instead, so callers handle just one kind. Stack catch blocks; the first match wins.

say.never: Put the `try` *inside* a loop and one bad item can't stop the rest. The catch block notes the problem, the loop moves on to the next item, and at the end you know how many went wrong.
say.bit: A try inside a loop: catch, count it, carry on with the next item.

say.never: A `finally` block goes after the catch blocks. It runs every time: when the try block finishes, when it throws, and even when it hits a `return`. That makes it the place for clean-up that must never be skipped, like turning the oven off.
say.bit: `finally` runs whether the try block finishes, throws or returns: the place for clean-up.

steps.title: In your lesson: Catch one, throw another

say.never: In `parseLine`, the three `Integer.parseInt` calls and `new ScoutEntry(...)` go in a try block. Catch the `NumberFormatException` and the `IllegalArgumentException`, and throw a `BadLineException` from each. (A `NumberFormatException` is a kind of `IllegalArgumentException`, so if you write both, the `NumberFormatException` catch goes first.) Then in `parseAll`, the try goes inside the loop: catch `BadLineException`, record the line number, and keep going.
say.bit: `parseLine`: catch the two exceptions and throw `BadLineException`. `parseAll`: try inside the loop, catch, `addBadLine`, keep going.

steps.title: In your lesson: finally always runs

say.never: `SafeAuto.runStep` runs one auto step. If the gyro is unplugged, the step throws after it has already started the wheels. Without `finally`, the robot would keep driving across the field. Return `true` from the try block, `false` from the catch block, and call `drive.stop()` in `finally`.
say.bit: `runStep`: return true from try, false from catch, `drive.stop()` in finally.
